result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description says a process begins when a participant performs an identifiable action that establishes the process trigger: Model a start event for the trigger, followed by a separate task for the participant’s action; do not represent the action only as a start event.

When the description says that the process waits for a stated time or period to end before continuing: Model the wait as an intermediate catch timer event, then connect it to the subsequent activity rather than representing the passage of time as a task.

When the description says that a process may continue only after an external participant approves a proposal: Model the approval wait as an intermediate catch event after the proposal is provided and before the dependent activity; preserve that order rather than modeling the wait as a task.

When the description says an activity occurs repeatedly or continues over an ongoing process and separately states that another activity starts only when a condition occurs: do not model the ongoing activity as an unconditional predecessor of the condition-triggered activity; preserve their distinct timing and stated dependencies in the BPMN flow
